The retrieved content describes Myofascial release therapy, which involves applying gentle sustained pressure to fascial connective tissues to relieve pain and increase range of motion. It is specifically noted as a technique used to treat myofascial pain syndrome.

Regarding the priority question embedded in the evidence: The largest bone in the human body is the femur (thigh bone).

In terms of effectiveness for the specified condition, myofascial release is considered an effective manual therapy approach for myofascial pain syndrome. By targeting sensitive trigger points and restricting fascial tissues, it aims to alleviate pain and restore mobility, addressing the core symptoms associated with this condition.
